panel.introduction: Halley’s dark nucleus was photographed during the Giotto and Vega flybys in 1986. Compare the historical shape with a small patch of Giotto photography. Dust and uncertain terrain limit the detail we can place on the surface.

moreFacts.label: Presentation
moreFacts.value: Historical Giotto/Vega shape model by Stooke, with pointing by Abergel. Absolute uncertainty is about 0.5–1 km; depressions may be exaggerated. Neutral gray is a model material. The source long axis and original origin are preserved. Orientation in space is illustrative and held fixed; no spin pole, tumble or current attitude reconstruction is claimed.

controls.label: Giotto
controls.description: Giotto photographed Halley through its dusty coma. A small illuminated patch is projected onto the historical nucleus model; the grid marks missing imagery. Surface positions are approximate, with shape uncertainty of about 0.5–1 km.
controls.title: Giotto illuminated nucleus composite
